slides.title: Social Simulations: from Agent-Based Modeling to Digital Twins
slides.highlight: This work explores the transition from classical agent-based models to LLM-enhanced simulations and Social Digital Twins, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: A survey tracing the evolution of social simulations from classical agent-based modeling to LLM-enhanced digital twins.
card.key_idea: Integrates rule-based Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) with LLM-driven reasoning and data-driven Social Digital Twins to simulate complex human interactions and socio-technical systems with higher fidelity.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the text is a survey reviewing existing literature, architectures, and theoretical frameworks rather than a new empirical study.
card.limitation: High computational costs, sensitivity to prompt design, and risks of overfitting or mistaking model biases for realistic human behavior.

slides.title: Faraday Future Launches FF Nexus Academy Summer Camps
slides.highlight: Faraday Future is implementing embodied AI robotics education through summer camps, which aligns with RwB's focus on embodied learning.

slides.title: China unveils humanoid AI 'companion robots' to ease loneliness
slides.highlight: The development of humanoid AI companion robots to address loneliness is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: On the Structure of Address in Multi-Party Dialogue: From Discrete Labels to Continuous Levels
slides.tldr: CONTINUOUS ADDRESSEE DETECTION IN MULTI-PARTY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This work explores addressee detection as a continuous phenomenon rather than discrete labels, analyzing its relationship with listener behaviors like gaze and backchannels, which is relevant to HyECHO's addressee and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Address in multi-party dialogue is better modeled as a continuous level than as discrete labels.
card.key_idea: A latent-variable model transforms categorical annotator judgments into continuous address levels, representing addressivity as a graded property rather than a multi-class classification task.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Japanese triadic dialogue corpus using GLMMs; continuous levels showed better predictive fit (ELPD) for turn-taking, gaze, and backchannels.
card.limitation: Limited to Japanese triadic discussions; address levels were inferred from only three categorical annotations per turn.

slides.title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game
slides.highlight: This research examines how mutual and referential robot gaze affects human visual attention during a collaborative game, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Robot gaze orientation does not significantly affect human visual attention during a cognitively demanding collaborative game.
card.key_idea: A NAO robot used LLM-driven dialogue in a word association game to test if mutual or referential gaze influenced human fixation times and confirmation-seeking behavior.
card.evaluation: 10 non-native English speakers were tested using Tobii Glasses 3. Results showed no significant effect of robot gaze on time to first fixation.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=10) and high cognitive load from non-native language use may have skewed results.

slides.title: PACE: Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC PERSONA ADAPTATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for humanoid robots to dynamically synthesize tailored, psychologically grounded personas through user interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and HRI.

card.one_liner: PACE enables humanoid robots to dynamically synthesize tailored personas through interactive user Q&A for improved HRI.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using adaptive Q&A to extract psychological dimensions, compiling them into a structured PersonaSpec that governs both LLM dialogue and Ameca robot's multimodal facial expressions.
card.evaluation: Tested with 25 participants against a static baseline using BFI-44, economic games, and Likert scales; results showed significant gains in trust and persona consistency.
card.limitation: Relies on cloud-based inference and ASR, potentially introducing latency and transcription errors in noisy environments.

slides.title: Forgetting Our Way to Shared Meaning: Effects of Forgetting on Conceptual Alignment in a Non-Partnership Coordination Game
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF MEMORY DEGRADATION ON CONCEPTUAL ALIGNMENT
slides.highlight: This research examines how memory characteristics and adaptiveness influence the emergence of shared meaning in non-partnership coordination games, providing insights for agent-based societal-scale simulation in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Adaptive memory improves actual conceptual alignment but leads agents to underestimate their shared meaning.
card.key_idea: A non-partnership coordination game using Voronoi tessellations to model conceptual regions, comparing adaptive agents with non-adaptive agents experiencing memory degradation.
card.evaluation: Counterfactual simulations with varying prototypes (3-10), adaptiveness (1-10%), and degradation rates. Results show adaptive players converge faster and closer.
card.limitation: Simulations used only two-player interactions; mixing memory types and complex network structures were not explored.

slides.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to derive whole-body tactile sensing requirements from VR-based interaction data, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A requirement-driven framework using VR to determine optimal tactile sensor placement and resolution for social robots.
card.key_idea: VR-based interaction data is collected to reconstruct contact geometry, allowing researchers to simulate and optimize sensor coverage and spatial resolution before physical hardware fabrication.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a 5,520-trial dataset with 18 participants using Random Forest and CNN-GRU classifiers; leave-one-subject-out cross-validation was used.
card.limitation: Simulations use binary contact signals (no force/pressure) and were conducted only on a single robot's arm in VR.

slides.title: Real-time Generation of Listener Nodding via Prediction of Kinematic Parameters for Avatar Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This research proposes a model for predicting the timing and kinematic parameters of listener nodding in real time, contributing to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A real-time model predicting both the timing and kinematic parameters of listener nodding for conversational avatars.
card.key_idea: Uses a dyadic attention network with Continuous Mimi Encoders; timing is learned via multi-task learning, and kinematic parameters are predicted by fine-tuning the timing module.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via five-fold cross-validation and subjective user studies (n=60) against stochastic and fixed baselines; results showed significant improvements in naturalness and attentiveness.
card.limitation: Subjective evaluations were conducted via pre-recorded videos as third-party observers rather than through direct, face-to-face interactions.

slides.title: CausalGraphX: A Counterfactual Graph Neural Network Framework for Explainable Systemic Risk Assessment
slides.tldr: EXPLAINABLE SYSTEMIC RISK ASSESSMENT VIA COUNTERFACTUAL GNNs
slides.highlight: CausalGraphX integrates Graph Neural Networks with counterfactual reasoning to model causal drivers of cascading failures in interconnected networks. This approach to simulating systemic risk and shock propagation aligns with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: CausalGraphX uses counterfactual GNNs to predict and explain systemic financial risk and cascading defaults.
card.key_idea: Combines Graph Attention Networks with adversarial regularization to learn causal representations and an optimization-based generator to produce sparse, actionable counterfactual interventions for risk mitigation.
card.evaluation: Tested on large-scale synthetic ER and BA networks against LR, DebtRank, GCN, and GAT; outperformed baselines in AUC, F1, and explanation plausibility.
card.limitation: Evaluation relies on synthetic datasets and simulators rather than real-world financial data due to data scarcity.

slides.title: CF-Net: Conflict Fusion with Speaker Normalisation and Certainty Weighting for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition
slides.highlight: CF-Net uses a ConflictFusion module and speaker normalization to detect ambivalence and hesitancy via cross-modal incongruence, supporting HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: CF-Net recognizes ambivalence and hesitancy by explicitly modeling cross-modal incongruence using frozen multimodal backbones.
card.key_idea: Uses ConflictFusion (pairwise absolute-difference features), per-speaker normalization to remove identity offsets, and certainty-weighted focal loss with an auxiliary regression head to handle annotation ambiguity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the BAH dataset; achieved 0.7155 validation Macro F1 and 0.7364 private test Macro F1, surpassing previous non-ensemble frozen-backbone models.
card.limitation: Relies on frozen backbones; future work suggests selective fine-tuning or replacing fixed fusion with learned cross-modal attention.

slides.title: ERR@HRI 3.0 Challenge: Multimodal Detection of Errors and Anticipation in Human-Robot Interactions
slides.highlight: This research introduces datasets for detecting bystander reactions and anticipatory facial responses to robot failures, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction quality.

card.one_liner: The ERR@HRI 3.0 Challenge introduces datasets for multimodal error detection and anticipation in human-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Two raw video datasets (BAD and Bad Idea) enable end-to-end ML models to detect bystander reactions and predict anticipatory facial responses to failures.
card.evaluation: Three teams submitted models that outperformed CNN baselines using crowdsourced, naturalistic video data from 45 and 29 participants.
card.limitation: The inherent variability of real-world, non-anonymized crowdsourced data presents a significant challenge for model robustness.

slides.title: Risk-Aware Preference Learning for Stochastic Outcomes
slides.highlight: This research explores using Cumulative Prospect Theory instead of expected utility to better model human risk sensitivity in social robot navigation. It is relevant to RwB for improving how embodied social robots align their behavior with user expectations regarding safety-critical outcomes.

card.one_liner: Modeling human risk sensitivity using Cumulative Prospect Theory improves reward learning for stochastic robot outcomes.
card.key_idea: Replaces linear Expected Utility with Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT) in a Bradley-Terry framework to capture nonlinear probability weighting and asymmetric loss aversion during preference learning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 2D social navigation simulations with synthetic EU and CPT users; CPT learners showed lower action regret for risk-sensitive users.
card.limitation: Results are based on synthetic users; human-subject validation has not yet been performed.

slides.title: Human-Robot Interaction in GenAI Architectures via the Agent-Client Protocol
slides.highlight: This paper proposes the Agent-Client Protocol (ACP) to standardize the HRI layer in agent-based robotic systems, enabling real-time human-in-the-loop collaboration. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A decoupled three-layer robotic architecture using ACP and MCP to standardize human-robot interaction and execution.
card.key_idea: Combines the Agent-Client Protocol (ACP) for the HRI layer and Model Context Protocol (MCP) for the execution layer, separating user interfaces, cognitive orchestration, and physical control.
card.evaluation: Tested on a physical mobile robot (Sancho) with three heterogeneous interfaces; results showed negligible latency overhead (<0.5% of total loop time).
card.limitation: ACP lacks native support for continuous multimodal data streaming (e.g., live camera feeds) and asynchronous background telemetry.
